title: # App startup
- When the app is launched:
- The left pane is opened by default
- An empty project is setup by default (empty object list, empty screen, dummy title at the top)
- The audio timeline shows a duration of zero
# Pane resizing
- When the user resizes the left pane:
- The right pane resizes accordingly
- The right pane cannot be fully closed by resizing
- The left pane fully closes when resized close to zero width
- The left pane can be reopened after being fully closed
- When the user resizes the object pane:
- None of the panes can be fully closed by resizing
# Project settings icon
- When the user opens the project settings:
- The project settings dialog appears
- The user can change the FPS
- The FPS cannot be set to less than 1
- The user can change the resolution
- The user cannot set a width or height of less than 1
- The user can pick an audio file by selecting a file in a file dialog, after clicking a button
- The user can bake FFT data by clicking a button
- The user cannot bake FFT data if no audio file is selected
- The progress is shown in a text format
- The user can close the project settings dialog
# New project icon
- When the user clicks the new project icon:
- A new empty project is created
- The object list is empty
- The screen is empty
- The project title at the top is set to a dummy title
- The audio timeline shows a duration of zero
# Open project icon
- When the user clicks the open project icon:
- A file dialog appears
- When the user selects a valid project file and confirms:
- The screen is locked and a progress bar as well as contextual text is shown
- The selected project is loaded, replacing the current project
- The screen is unlocked and the progress bar and contextual text disappear
- The project title at the top is updated to the opened project's title
- The object list is updated to the opened project's objects
- The screen is updated to the opened project's screen
- The audio timeline is updated to the opened project's audio file
- When the user cancels the file dialog:
- No changes are made to the current project
# Save project icon
- When the user clicks the save project icon:
- A file dialog opens up and the user can pick a file name
- A native warning appears if the selected file already exists
- When the user confirms the file dialog:
- The screen is locked and a progress bar as well as contextual text is shown
- The current project is saved to the selected file
- The screen is unlocked and the progress bar and contextual text disappear
- The asterisk indicating unsaved changes disappears from the project title at the top
- When the user cancels the file dialog:
- No changes are made to the current project
# Settings icon
- When the user clicks the settings icon:
- The settings dialog appears
- The user can change the application theme between light and dark (immediate effect)
- The user can change the application language (immediate effect)
- The user can see the logs location path after clicking a button
- The path seem to be the right one
- The user can close the settings dialog

# New object icon
- When the user clicks the new object icon:
- A dialog appears with a list of object types to choose from
- When the user clicks on an object type:
- The dialog closes
- A new object of the selected type is added at the end of the object list
- The new object is visible on the screen
- When the user cancels the new object dialog:
- No new object is added to the object list

# Object list
- The object list is scrollable if the objects do not fit in the pane
- When the user clicks on an object in the object list:
- The clicked object is selected
- The selected object's properties can be edited in the pane underneath the object list, with its name visible at the top
# Shape visual object
- When a shape visual object is selected:
- The user can change its name
- The user can change its layer (Z index)
- The user can change its size (width and height >= 0)
- A zero width or height do not create unexpected behaviour or errors
- Shortcut buttons behave correctly (full width, etc.)
- The user can change its position (X and Y)
- The shortcut buttons behave correctly
- The user can change its rotation (in degrees)
- The user can change its border radius
- The user can change its box shadow
- The user can change its background type between color, gradient and image
- The setting for each type is persistent and restored when switching between types
- When colour is selected:
- The user can change the background colour
- When gradient is selected:
- The user can change the gradient
- When image is selected:
- The user can pick an image file by selecting a file in a file dialog, after clicking a button
- The user can change the image fit mode
- When the user selects scale size control:
- The user can change the scale using a newly shown input field
- The scale input field is hidden when selecting another fit mode
- When the user selects width height size control:
- The user can change the width and height using newly shown input fields
- The width and height input fields are hidden when selecting another fit mode
- The user can change the image repeat mode

# Audio controls"
- When the user clicks the play button:
- The project playback starts from the current timeline position
- The play button changes to a pause button
- When the user clicks the pause button:
- The project playback pauses
- The pause button changes to a play button
- When the user clicks the 'to start' button:
- The timeline position moves to the start (0:00)
- When the user clicks the 'to end' button:
- The timeline position moves to the end (project duration)
- The playback stops if it was playing and loop mode is disabled
- The playback moves to the start if it was playing and loop mode is enabled
- When the user toggles the loop mode button:
- The loop mode is enabled/disabled accordingly
- When the user drags the timeline position slider:
- The timeline position moves accordingly
- The playback updates accordingly
- When the user clicks the fast forward button:
- The timeline position moves forward by 5 seconds
- The playback updates accordingly
- When the user clicks the rewind button:
- The timeline position moves backward by 5 seconds
- The playback updates accordingly
